How long does it take to build a deck?
Most standard decks take 1–2 weeks to complete, depending on size, design complexity, and weather. Larger custom decks or multi-level builds may take 3 weeks or more.
Do you handle permits?

Yes. Ottawa DeckPro can prepare permit drawings and submit all required documents to the City of Ottawa or nearby municipalities. We make sure your deck meets all building-code and zoning requirements.
What areas do you serve?

What materials do you build with?
We specialize in pressure-treated, cedar, composite, and PVC decking, paired with modern aluminum or glass railings. All materials are selected for durability in Ottawa’s climate.
How much does a new deck cost?
Decks typically start around $7,000 – $12,000 for basic builds and can exceed $35,000+ for large or high-end designs. Material choice, layout, and site access all influence pricing.
What’s the difference between composite and PVC decking?
Composite is a blend of wood fibers and plastic, durable and low-maintenance.
PVC is 100 % plastic, completely waterproof, and offers the longest lifespan with minimal fading.
Do you offer free estimates?
Yes! We provide free on-site estimates and digital proposals. You can book yours through our website or by calling 613-639-1744.
Can I customize my deck design?
Absolutely. Every deck is custom-built. We can integrate stairs, skirting, lighting, privacy screens, and railing combinations to match your home and lifestyle.

Pressure-treated: 10 – 15 years

Yes, we handle demolition and disposal of existing decks before construction. We leave your property clean and ready for use.

Typically every 2 – 3 years, depending on sun exposure and product used. We use premium coatings designed for Ottawa’s weather.

Deciding between a composite deck and a wood deck is one of the first steps when planning an outdoor living space in Ottawa. Choosing the right decking material affects not only the look and feel of your deck but also its durability and maintenance over time. This guide compares composite decking and wood decks to help you make an informed decision for your home.
What is a Wood Deck?

A wood deck is built using natural lumber, commonly cedar, pine, or pressure-treated wood. Wood decks have been a traditional choice for decades due to their natural beauty and warmth. The grain patterns and textures of wood create a classic outdoor aesthetic that many homeowners appreciate.

Wood decks require regular maintenance to protect against Ottawa’s climate. This includes sealing, staining, or painting every few years to prevent moisture damage, warping, and insect infestation. While wood decks can be more affordable upfront, the ongoing upkeep is a key consideration.
What is Composite Decking?

Composite decking is made from a blend of wood fibers and recycled plastic. This combination creates a material designed to mimic the appearance of wood while offering enhanced durability. Composite decking is engineered to resist fading, staining, and moisture damage better than natural wood.

In Ottawa, composite decking is popular because it withstands harsh winters and fluctuating temperatures without cracking or splintering. It also requires less maintenance, as it does not need sealing or staining. Many composite decking options come with built-in UV protection and textured surfaces for slip resistance.

Wood decks generally have a lower initial cost. Composite decking costs more upfront but can save money over time due to reduced maintenance.
Maintenance
Wood decks need regular sealing, staining, and inspections for rot or insect damage. Composite decks require only occasional cleaning with soap and water.
Durability
Composite decking resists moisture, fading, and temperature changes better than wood. Wood can warp, crack, or splinter if not properly maintained.
Appearance
Wood offers a natural, authentic look with unique grain patterns. Composite decking provides consistent color and texture, with options that closely resemble wood.
Which is Better for Ottawa’s Climate?

Ottawa’s climate poses challenges for any outdoor structure. Winters bring freezing temperatures and snow, while spring and fall can be wet and humid. These conditions cause wood to expand, contract, and sometimes deteriorate faster.

Composite decking is better suited for Ottawa’s climate because it handles moisture and temperature changes without warping or rotting. It also resists mold and mildew growth, common issues in humid conditions. Wood decks can last many years but require vigilant maintenance to protect against the elements.
Cost Comparison

While composite decks are more expensive upfront, they reduce costs related to maintenance, repairs, and refinishing over time. Wood decks may require sealing every 2-3 years, which adds to the lifetime expense.

Long-term Value and Maintenance

For homeowners who prefer spending weekends enjoying their deck rather than maintaining it, composite decking is a practical choice. Wood decks appeal to those who value natural materials and are willing to invest time in upkeep.
